title: Separating and analysing - 123 school
heading: Separating and analysing
intro: Choose the correct answer for each question. Where BINAS is mentioned, look up the data in the table named. Use a calculator where needed.

questions.question: Which separation method do you use to remove sand from water?
Which separation method do you use to obtain pure water from sea water?
What is distillation based on?
What is filtration based on?
What is extraction based on?
What is settling based on?
You want to remove a dye from a solution with activated carbon. What is this called?
How do you separate iron filings from sand?
A suspension is a mixture of …
What is a pure substance?

answers.a: a substance that dissolves in water
answers.b: a substance without colour and smell
answers.c: a substance with always the same properties, such as a fixed melting point

questions.question: What do you use chromatography for?

answers.b: to determine the mass of a substance
answers.c: to separate and recognise the substances in a mixture
answers.d: to measure the temperature of a mixture

questions.question: What is the stationary phase in paper chromatography?
What is the mobile phase in paper chromatography?
In which BINAS table is chromatography found?
How do you draw the starting line in paper chromatography?
What is the formula for the Rf value?
A substance travels 3.0 cm and the solvent 6.0 cm. What is the Rf value?
A substance travels 2.4 cm and the solvent 8.0 cm. What is the Rf value?
A substance has Rf = 0.40 and the solvent has travelled 10.0 cm. How far has the substance travelled?
Which Rf value cannot occur?
Two spots have the same Rf value on the same paper. What does that probably mean?

answers.a: the substance has not dissolved yet

questions.question: On a chromatogram of an ink mixture you see three spots. What does that mean?

answers.b: the ink consists of one substance
answers.d: the ink contains at least three substances

questions.question: What is the retention time in gas chromatography?

answers.a: the time the instrument needs to warm up
answers.c: the distance of the substance divided by the distance of the solvent
answers.d: the time a substance needs to travel through the column

questions.question: In a gas chromatogram peak A has a larger area than peak B. What does that mean?

answers.a: there is more of substance A in the mixture than of substance B
answers.b: substance A has a longer retention time than substance B
answers.c: substance A is purer than substance B
answers.d: substance A boils at a higher temperature than substance B

questions.question: What is a calibration line?

answers.a: a line on a measuring cylinder
answers.b: a graph of temperature against time
answers.c: a line that shows the pH
answers.d: a graph of a measured value against the known concentration

questions.question: What do you use a calibration line for?

answers.a: to calculate the mass of a substance
answers.c: to measure the pH of an acid

questions.question: For a calibration line you measure the absorbance of solutions with known concentrations. What do you put on the horizontal axis?
What is titration?

answers.b: adding a solution of known concentration until the reaction is exactly complete
answers.c: weighing a substance on a balance
answers.d: heating a mixture until it boils

questions.question: In a titration the burette reading at the start is 12.45 mL and at the end 24.72 mL. How many mL was added?
What is a burette used for in a titration?

answers.a: adding dropwise and reading the volume added
answers.c: measuring the pH without an indicator

questions.question: What do you use an indicator for in a titration?

answers.d: to see the colour change when the reaction is complete

questions.question: How many moles are present in 20.0 mL of a solution with c = 0.100 mol/L?
25.0 mL of HCl needs 20.0 mL of 0.100 mol/L NaOH (HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H<sub>2</sub>O). What is c(HCl)?
10.0 mL of NaOH needs 15.0 mL of 0.200 mol/L HCl (HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H<sub>2</sub>O). What is c(NaOH)?
